sentences: A young woman clings to a man with both arms, while he, wrapped in what looks like a monk's robe, stares into empty space.
Egon Schiele painted this picture in 1915, and the man is a self-portrait.
The woman is Wally Neuzil, his partner and model for several years, whom Schiele left in order to marry Edith Harms, a woman from a respectable middle-class family.
Soon after the wedding he was called up for service in the First World War, and in his work of this period death and love often appear together.
The couple's unstable pose shows a fragile balance that seems ready to break at any moment.
Schiele first called the picture Man and Girl and also Entwined People, and the title Death and the Maiden borrows a theme that goes back to the Renaissance.
After their separation Wally trained as a nurse and died of scarlet fever in 1917 while serving in the war.
The painting is now in the Belvedere in Vienna.
